notes: One file now installs the radio and the same file updates it: download Win - Install or Update Deskside Radio.cmd, double-click it, and it fetches the release, unpacks it beside the browser profile it already uses, writes the Desktop shortcut and opens the radio. It ships inside the zip too, so after the first run a copy is always in the app folder and updating is double-clicking it -- no administrator, no UAC prompt, and nothing running in the background. The radio also says when there is an update instead of waiting to be asked: a discreet notice in the top bar, a check every six hours, and a Check now button in Settings that reports what it found. Settings settles its height once as it opens, against its tallest pane, capped at three quarters of the desktop rather than of its own window, and it arrives rather than appears. Cards fold shut instead of snapping, and Stations saves and collapses the way Schedule does. The volume control now follows a scheduled fade, so the knob moves with what you are hearing. The schedule pilot reads green in every theme and its chip says what happens next in the theme's own voice. Eight themes' worth of smaller work: the analogue meter is lit from its own bulb and its card, numerals and badges are set properly; Marconi's scale can be read and its pointer wears deco jewellery; the console readout flickers the way a tired VFD does; the 8-bit meter lights whole LEDs and never half of one; Model One's transport is a knob; and a preset's name has room to be drawn in and scrolls more slowly when there is more of it than will fit. The chosen theme is marked by one flag, the same on all eight, instead of eight that each disappear into their own artwork.
